title: fix(app): generator refusals speak the document's unit (#740)
body:
An inch document's refusals still read millimeters: a bore 25 mm too deep was refused as `25.000 mm deep`, a `Ø14 shank in a Ø12 hole` quoted bare millimeters - while every dialog around it spoke inches (#740).

## The change

The refusal sentences are built deep in the generator, off the worker threads, world-free - that's why they never saw the document's unit. The fix carries the unit to them rather than reaching for the world:

- `GenJob` grows a `unit: Unit` field; `collect_job` fills it from `crate::units::of(world)` while the world is still in hand, and it rides into every refusal builder as one added argument (`too_deep`, `shank_fits`, `axial_reach`, the cross-reach family in `cross_spindle`/`cross_stock`/`cross_holder`, `circle_of_region`, `pocket_region_on_part`/`around_part`, `offset_run`). `AreaCtx` carries it the same way.
- The lens itself: `units::len(v_mm, unit, prec)` prints `{:.prec}` byte-identically in millimeters and the converted value at `prec + 2` in inches; `Unit::suffix()` gives the word. Every pinned number is `{:.3}` in mm, so inch refusals read five decimals. Where the sentence had a literal `" mm"` it now ends `units::len(..) + unit.suffix()`; bare numbers (mouth coordinates, `shank dia. {:.3}`, `Z {:.3}`) become suffixless `units::len(..)`.
- `GenError::At`'s location stays millimeters - the lens is for the sentence, not the geometry marker. Tests pin this.
- Two `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` attrs (`axial_reach`, `shank_fits`), following the existing convention in `generate.rs`/`plunge_solid.rs`.

Millimeter documents change not one byte: the existing suite, which pins these sentences verbatim, passes untouched.

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

`crates/app/tests/units_in_refusals.rs` runs five operations twice each, mm then inch, asserting the mm sentence byte-for-byte and the inch sentence converted:

- `an_axial_reach_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - through-hole `too_deep`: depth, flute, fix depth cross the lens, ` mm` becomes ` in`.
- `a_cross_reach_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - raw-bar cross hole: mouth coords `(10.000, 0.000, 0.000)` -> `(0.39370, 0.00000, 0.00000)`; the `At` location is pinned to stay `(10, 0, 0)` mm.
- `a_shank_fit_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - the BR-1000 shank refusal: depth/flute lensed, bare `shank dia. 14.000` -> `0.55118`; location pinned mm.
- `a_circle_fit_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - circular-fit deviation and centre point.
- `a_part_fills_the_selection_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - the plane named in the area refusal: ` at Z 7.000` -> ` at Z 0.27559`.

## Scope, relative to the claim table

- `material::section()`'s refusal is dead code - dropped.
- The `holder()` raw-`Display` refusal and the pure-crate refusals (`camcraft-tools`, `camcraft-motion`) need their unit plumbed through crate APIs, not job args - a follow-up PR.
- Refusals quoting profile constants (`spun`, `holder_profile`, `lathe_holder`) quote tool definitions, not document measurements - left alone.
- The contour travel *note* (`contour: rides the open boundary 0.400 mm...`) is a note, not a refusal - left for the same follow-up.

## Tested

- Red first: with only the pins committed, `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test units_in_refusals` builds clean and all five fail on the millimeter strings they still see.
- Green: same command, 5 passed, 0 failed.
- The mm byte-identity proof: untouched sentence pins across the drilling/area/pick suites all pass unmodified - lib `drill_reach` (8), `area::` (4), `contour_open` (2), and integration binaries `drill_reach`, `drill_reach_fit`, `drilling_cross_holder`, `drilling_cross_spindle`, `drilling_cross_stock`, `drilling_cross_rapids`, `drilling_axial`, `circular_pick`, `pick_agnostic`, `drilling_cross`, `drilling_cross_box`, `drilling_cross_part`, `drill_prior`, `drill_prior_kinds`, `drill_rplane`, `lathe_cross_drill`, `area_controls`, `area_open`, `area_picks`, `whole_model_pocket`, `boundary_walls`, `probe_pick`, `refusal_location`, `pick`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` finishes clean.
- Not exercised: the other crates - the fix touches only `camcraft-app`.

Changelog: generator refusals now print their numbers in the document's unit - an inch document reads inches, millimeter documents unchanged (#740)

Fixes #740

  content.

- New `crates/app/tests/orient_dropdowns.rs` (9 tests): a tilted

define the full 3D frame.

- `pick::align_from_axes` (`crates/app/src/pick/axis.rs`): with both

  picks' cross, the right-hand rule. The part turns about the centre
  of its bounds; the origin is NOT set (the work offset stays where
  it is placed). A left-handed pair is honoured literally (the part
  lands as picked) instead of refused; only (nearly) parallel picks

- New `crates/app/tests/align_axes.rs` (9 tests): the user's exact

body:
## What changed

Phase 1 of #763: **`OpFrame`** — the one machining-frame seam in
`crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs` — composes the two existing frame
mechanisms (the setup's `part_alignment` from #326 and the op's 3+2
`Tilt` from M5.1 B) behind one door, and `collect_job` reads through it:

- `OpFrame::of(op)` built once per generation; material and heights
  resolve through it; the tilt frame comes from
  `OpFrame::checked_frame` — one construction site, the refusal keeping
  its exact words and its exact precedence (after the heights resolve,
  the job's error-order law).
- The contract is stated once in the module header: D / S / L frames,
  right-to-left composition `p_L = T(A(p_D))`, the CL wrapping back via
  `TiltedFrame::world_path` (identity clone without a tilt), and the
  furniture law (stock / WCS / fixtures live in S: never aligned, but
  read local by the tilt).
- Heights and bounds in L ship correct from day one
  (`aabb_local_of`, `height_z_local`): they resolve against FULLY
  TRANSFORMED geometry, never a `z − origin.z` shift of the S box —
  the shift is only correct while the tool axis is the world Z.

**No refusal lifted, no post change, no generator change.** The four
verified kinds, picks, area controls and tilt-in-aligned-setups keep
their refusals; the later phases lift them one by one, each with its
numeric pin.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/opframe_seam.rs` (8 tests) + the seam's inline
  unit tests (6): identity passthrough; zero-tilt index reproduces the
  prismatic path EXACTLY move-for-move (the identity-bits law); a
  tilted face runs in its own plane (every endpoint maps back into the
  L1-folded height band over the local silhouette, tool axis =
  hand-computed Rx(45)); 90-degree alignment turns the solid and its
  TopOfModel height (15, not 10); 180-degree alignment mirrors the
  facets by hand math; alignment × tilt composition pinned against
  hand-composed transforms; local heights/boxes read fully transformed
  geometry (and provably NOT the z-shift); picks stay refused by name
  while the door Phase 2 will read through is already aligned.
- Capability gates: unchanged by design; the tilted-move refusal keeps
  its existing verbatim pin in `tests/inverted_post.rs`.
- The four kinds' aligned generation keeps its pins in the #326 suites
  (`plane_align`, `axis_align`, `rest_across_setups`, …), run by the
  same gate.

## What was not exercised

- The L-frame height/AABB resolve methods are pinned by tests only —
  no production call site switches onto them until Phase 2+ lifts the
  matching refusals (deliberate: the seam lands behavior-identical).
- The boundary/region builders (`boundary_ctx`, `material_region`,
  `boundary_picks`) still build their own frames from `op.params.tilt()`
  — they move onto the seam in the later phases.

title: fix(xtask): test scanner ignores braces in strings, chars and comments
body:
## What changed
`xtask/src/scan.rs` `test_fns` ended each test span by counting every `{`/`}`, including those inside string literals, so `refuse("{", "bad JSON")` in `fixture_library.rs` swallowed the next test and `cargo xtask gate test <next test>` reported "no #[test] fn matches".

The depth count now goes through the new `xtask/src/braces.rs`, which skips braces inside `"..."` (with `\\` and `\"` escapes), raw strings (`r"..."`, `r#"..."#`, any number of `#`), char literals (`'{'`, `'\''`, `'\u{7d}'`; lifetimes like `'a` are left alone) and `//` comments. The lexer state carries across lines, so multi-line strings work. No unwrap/expect/panic.

The quick tier's changed-fn picker uses the same `test_fns` spans, so it is fixed by the same change.

## How tested
- `cargo test -p xtask`: 30 passed (3 new), `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- Pinning tests: `braces_in_string_literals_do_not_swallow_the_next_test`, `braces_in_raw_strings_chars_comments_and_lifetimes_are_ignored`, `a_change_in_the_test_after_a_brace_string_is_attributed_to_it` (quick planner: a hunk in the second test plans `--exact second`).
- Repro commands from the issue, with `--dry-run`: `the_library_folder_is_the_override_else_a_sibling_of_machines` before: "no #[test] fn matches"; after: `app fixture_library  dry run`. `a_bad_library_is_refused_whole_by_name` finds its test as before.

## Not exercised
Block comments (`/* { */`) are not skipped (not in the issue's scope). Full batch/release tiers not run (tooling only).

## Process
`xtask/` is a process file: `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` bumped 10 -> 11. A fork must do nothing beyond the normal process sync. Fork synced at v0.16.0.

Implement manual-backed TNC DIN/ISO G200/G205/G206/G207 drilling/tapping cycles and G247 preset activation. Documented Q values distinguish absolute origin-relative surface coordinates from incremental depth/clearance. One-shot M99 calls replace only the expanded axial cuts; explicit safe links remain. No invented G80 or modal M89.

Add an explicit **Floating tap** operation choice alongside rigid **Tap**, through normal editing/undo, persisted parameters/cached cycles, CL/CNC serialization, UI and script exposure. Existing `tap`/`TAP` stays rigid. Only explicit floating-holder intent selects G206; `rigidTapping=false` refuses G207 and never implies floating tooling. Posts without the floating-tapping capability refuse that mode by name.

Source: HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 Cycle Programming 892905-25, English 9/2016, NC34059x-07, sections2.1,3.3,3.8,4.2,4.3,10.4; ISO Programming manual892909-25 for block/call form. - G200 drilling/full-return deep drilling; G205 constant chip-breaking pecks; G206 explicit floating-holder tapping; G207 rigid tapping with machine-capability refusal.

- Nonrepresentable R-to-entry PECK/DEEP intent retains its established explicit chain rather than deepening the first infeed. Boring chains and unrelated safety refusals remain.

title: test(app): fixture_library folder resolver uses host-absolute paths
body:
## What changed

`crates/app/tests/fixture_library.rs`, test `the_library_folder_is_the_override_else_a_sibling_of_machines` only. No product code.

The test fed Unix-only paths (`/shop/fixtures`, `/Users/me`, `/home/me`). `fixture_library::user_dir_for` (`store.rs`) keeps an override only when `PathBuf::is_absolute()` is true on the host, so on a Windows host those paths were dropped and the assertions failed.

- The override path, the macOS HOME and the linux HOME are now picked per OS with `cfg!(windows)` (`C:\shop\fixtures`, `C:\Users\me`, `C:\home\me` on Windows; the old strings elsewhere), the same pattern as `machine_edit.rs` `the_user_folder_resolves_from_the_override_else_the_platform_data_folder`.
- Expected folders are built with `PathBuf::from(home).join(...)`, so separators are right on both hosts.
- The `env` helper now copies its pairs into owned strings instead of requiring `&'static` literals, so runtime-chosen per-OS strings can be passed.
- Assertions keep their meaning: an absolute override wins; a relative override (`"relative"`) falls back to HOME; the macOS and linux data folders are unchanged; `linux` with no HOME gives `None`. `library_path(&PathBuf::from("/x"))` is unchanged: it only checks the file name suffix, which holds on any host.

## Why it passes on Windows

On Windows the three host-absolute paths are absolute, so `CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES` is kept and the HOME branches resolve under `C:\Users\me` / `C:\home\me`. The relative override stays non-absolute on Windows too, so it falls back to HOME. The expected `PathBuf`s are built from the same strings with `join`, so they compare equal to what `user_dir_for` produces. This is the same construction as `machine_edit.rs`, which already passes in the Windows batch.

## How tested

- macOS: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test fixture_library -- the_library_folder_is_the_override_else_a_sibling_of_machines --exact` - 1 passed.
- macOS: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test fixture_library -- -D warnings` - clean.

title: fix(ui,app): setup alignment composes on the current pose, one flow, readable picks (#738)
body:
## What changed (#738, maintainer-reported, P1)

1. **Moves compose on the current pose.** Laying on a face or on three points now computes the lay in the setup's current alignment and composes it onto that alignment, through new `pick::lay_on_plane_in` / `lay_on_points_in` and `setup_turn::held_centre`. Before, each move went back to the import pose first. Axes already composed. Each move is still one `AlignPartToSetup`, and one undo returns to the previous pose exactly. Re-applying the same pick is a zero step and is refused as "already holds the part that way".
2. **One flow.** The top row now reads "Part alignment - each move starts from where the part sits now", and its tooltip describes the flow.
   - "Start from a preset" presets turn the part from where it sits, and so does the typed "Turn by", through the new `CommandKind::TurnPart` → `AlignPartToSetup::turn_by`.
   - "As modelled" is the one reset.
   - The pickers' Apply tooltips say a move starts from the current pose and is one undo step.
3. **Readable status.** It now reads "1 face selected", "2 points selected" or "1 edge selected" (`pick_words`).
   - Points show where they are: "Point 2: on 'part' (x, y, z) mm".
   - Internal ids ("Face 0xccc7c…") never show; app refusals on the page are stripped of " 0x…".
4. **Picks you can see.** `align_pick_viz::paint`:
   - picked faces are filled with the pick violet (alpha 96);
   - picked points are 6 px filled discs;
   - picked edges are 4 px strokes.

**Splits, so no large file grows:**
- `commands/align_stock.rs` comes out of `setup_align.rs` (422 → 298 lines).
- `state_align.rs` comes out of `state.rs` (4116 → 4062 lines).
- No snapshot PNG changed.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/738-align-flow.md`.

## Pinned by
- `align_compose` (new, 3 tests):
  - axes then face;
  - face then three points;
  - turn-by after a lay, for both pivots, plus the zero and NaN refusals.

  Each checks that the second move composes on the first, and that undo, undo and redo step back exactly.
- `setup_align_tests::a_preset_after_a_face_lay_composes_and_as_modelled_is_the_one_reset` (real clicks, Ctrl+Z).
- `setup_plane_tests::the_pick_status_counts_the_face_and_never_shows_an_id` and `setup_points_tests::the_pick_status_counts_the_points_and_never_shows_an_id`.

body:
**Stacked on #676** (#670, plasma profile), which is stacked on #674 (#669, plasma kind). Review only this PR's own commit, `2645a023`.

A **PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL** (#671). Every word below was checked against UM10720 v1223A ([UM]) or Tormach's PathPilot Post Processor Guidelines, Plasma column ([PG]).

| Word | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `G20`/`G21` | units | [PG] |
| `G90 G91.1 G94 G17 G40 G49 G80` | modal reset, once | [PG]; [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G64 P0.005 Q0.005` | path blending (P in inches even under G21) | [UM] §6.2.1 p.50; [PG] |
| `G54` | work offset | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `G43 H1` | torch length offset | [PG] ("always H1"); [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G30` | go to the G30 height | [UM] §6.2.1-6.2.2 |
| `G0 X Y` | rapid to the pierce point, never Z | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `M200` | AutoFS (feed, THC volts, pierce height and delay, amps) | [UM] §6.3 p.51, §7.2 p.54 |
| `M207`/`M208`/`M209 P` | pierce height / cut height / pierce delay, only when the op states them | [UM] §6.3.1 p.52, §7.2 |
| `G15` | ohmic probe; WCS Z = 0 | [UM] §7.1 p.54 |
| `G16` | rise to pierce height, fire, delay, go to cut height, THC on | [UM] §7.1; [PG] |
| `G1/G2/G3 X Y [I J] [F]` | the cut, XY only | [PG] |
| `G41.1`/`G42.1 D<kerf>` … `G40` | control compensation, each on its own line before a straight lead | [PG] |
| `M205` | torch off, Z to the G30 height | [UM] §7.2 |
| `M30` | end | [PG] |

- **Never written:** S, M3-M9, M6, G95-G99, canned cycles.
- **M6 conflict:** [PG] says M6 is unsupported on plasma, but [UM]'s test program writes `T1 M6`. This follows the issue and [PG]; the conflict is recorded.

## What changed
- **Script:** `assets/posts/tormach-plasma.cps`, registered as "Tormach PathPilot Plasma", the only `PLASMA_POSTS` entry. Milling posts decline a plasma stream, because they lack the torch hooks.
- **Stream:** #676's records are carried into the post stream: `PLASMA …`, `TORCH ON C<id> …` and `TORCH OFF C<id>` (the `.cl` v5 records without `; `).
  - The parser reads both spellings; malformed records are refused by line number.
  - New properties: `PlasmaKerf`, `PlasmaCompensation`, `PierceHeight`, `CutHeight`, `PierceDelay` (absent = AutoFS), `PlasmaFeed`, `PlasmaReversed`, `Contour`, `ContourRole`, `ParentContour`, `SmallHole`.
  - New hooks: `onPlasma`, `onTorchOn`, `onTorchOff`.
  - `machine.kind` is now a script property.
- **Engine torch law** (`cnc_torch.rs`), refused by name:

  - ON while lit, a wrong or extra OFF, a rapid while lit;
  - a section or stream left lit;
  - a script without both torch hooks.
- **Post refusals:**
  - a non-plasma op, a Plasma Profile path with no plasma record;
  - rpm, coolant (other than off), a rotary or tilted move;
  - Z on a lit move, a canned cycle, a dark feed;
  - comp under a computer offset, wear comp;
  - a machine that isn't `kind: plasma`.
- **AutoFS:** under AUTOFEED, no F is written. A small hole then runs at the AutoFS feed, with an operator comment; refusing it would block every default plate with a hole.

title: feat(tools): align a vendor STEP by ISO 13399 tool coordinate systems
body:
Second slice of #370 (and part of #361): auto-aligning a vendor STEP by its ISO 13399 tool coordinate systems.

## What changed
- `ToolCsysReport::align_tool_body()` extracts the tool axis and tip offset (`-dot(origin, axis)`) strictly from CIP (coordinate system in process, ISO 13399-303 §3.3) so that the cutting reference point sits at Z = 0 in the tool frame, pointing up into the spindle along +Z. No fallback to CSIF is performed since CSIF denotes the mounting interface, not the cutting point; missing, ambiguous, or degenerate CIP refuses by name.
- `ToolBodySpec::from_step_auto(&path)` reads both mesh facets and coordinate systems from a vendor STEP file, aligning it with zero manual offsets. Stated non-mm length units (e.g. inches, cm) are normalized consistently across both geometry and coordinate systems via `step_units::mm_per_unit`.
- `SetToolBody::from_step_auto(&world, tool_name, &path)` attaches the auto-aligned tool body as one undoable command.
- `tool_body_view::load_aligned(&path)` returns `LoadedBody` carrying the auto-alignment result or fallback reason, preserving `load` backwards compatibility.
- In the tool editor (`ToolBodyUi`), importing a STEP file with ISO 13399 coordinate systems automatically sets the axis and tip offset with the note "aligned by ISO 13399 coordinate systems"; importing a file without them or with degenerate/ambiguous coordinate systems falls back to default numeric placement ([0, 0, 1] axis, 0 offset) with a note naming why.
- Manually editing the axis combo or tip offset in the UI clears the alignment note to avoid displaying stale provenance.
- Test fixture `testdata/models/tool_csys_box_iso13399.step` combining a B-rep box and ISO 13399 placements.
- `docs/decisions/370-tool-csys-align.md`.

Merged `upstream/main` and clean.

title: fix(post): an explicit M5 after a probe's tool change in every post
body:
Was stacked on #579 (#570, probe search limit and feed-only approach), which merged on 2026-11-10; this PR now holds only #574's change against main.

## What changed
Every mill post now writes an explicit spindle stop between a probe's tool change and length offset and its first move. Today the probe is safe on a Tormach only because PathPilot's `M6` stops the spindle, which is a property of the control, not something the program says.
- **Rule:** in `startPreamble`, `probeStop = spindleWait && !(sRpm > 0)`. Only a probe states 0 rpm, because tools refuse 0. After the spindle block and before coolant, the post writes the stop.
- **Per post:**

**Stack merge (`fd1076af`):** #579 branched from a main older than #174's protected probe moves, so merging it hit conflicts in three Fanuc goldens and broke `probe_guard`. The merge commit resolves both.
- #579's new feed from the safe plane down to the approach plane now posts as a protected move: `G31` plus the `#5063` alarm on Fanuc, `G38.3` plus the `#5070` check on Tormach.
- `probe_guard` expects one more protected move per mode.
- `fanuc/probe_corner.nc` and `tormach/probe_guard_moves.nc` are regenerated to match.

#579 will need the same resolution when it takes main.

**Golden diffs from #574 itself:** each file gains one `M5` line right after the `G43` line:
- `fanuc/probe_bore_centre.nc`
- `fanuc/probe_corner.nc`
- `fanuc/probe_corner_negative.nc`

Until #526 merges, some posts still write a probe's spindle start (`S0 M3`) before the new stop. The flag is computed separately, so it works in either merge order; Heidenhain will have a small hand-merge next to #526's lines.

title: feat(post): the document's program number and comment, per dialect (#258 part 2)
body:
Part 2 of #258's split: the program number and comment. Today every post hard-codes `O0001` followed by the machine name. Branched from upstream/main; the fork is synced at v0.15.0.

## What changed
- **Document field:** a new `ProgramInfo { number, comment }` singleton (schema.rs). Unset means every post writes exactly what it wrote before.
- **Command:** an undoable `SetProgramInfo`. At creation it refuses by name:
  - a number outside 1-9999;
  - a comment over 40 characters, non-printable or non-ASCII, or containing `( ) % ; *`.

  Chosen: refuse rather than sanitise. Heidenhain and SINUMERIK, which use the comment as the program name, check it against their name rules at post time.
- **UI:** "Program number" and "Program comment" fields on the Post page. They commit on Enter or when focus leaves.
- **MCP:** a new `set_program` tool.
- **Scripts:** they get a `program` global `{number, numbered, comment}` (`engine::run_program_with`); `programNumber` is kept. Documented in docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md.
- **Per-operation files:** one file per op counts up from the stated number and is refused past O9999. The old code silently clamped instead.
- **Project file v59:** an optional `program` key. This is a version step, not just an added key, because an older build would drop the key and post O0001, which could overwrite a different program on the control. v58 files load with nothing set.

**Per dialect.** Each rule is cited in its .cps. The manual section references were written from memory, so a maintainer may want to check them against the manuals.
- **Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak:** `O####` (O0001-O9999), then `(<comment or machine name>)`.
- **Haas:** five-digit `O#####`, written only when a number is set.
- **Tormach PathPilot:** never an O-word, because LinuxCNC's O words are subroutine and flow-control words. A number goes in the header comment.
- **Heidenhain ISO:** the comment becomes the program name, `%<name> G71 *`, limited to file-name characters. If only a number is set, it is used as the name.
- **SINUMERIK:** the comment becomes `%_N_<NAME>_MPF` (letters, digits and `_`; the first two are letters or `_` plus a letter; at most 24 characters). A name that breaks these rules is refused, not renamed. The number goes in a `; PROGRAM n` comment.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/258-program-number.md`.

## How tested
- **New `program_info` tests (9):**
  - output is byte-identical in all 7 posts when nothing is set;
  - each dialect's header with a number and comment, and with a number alone;
  - post-time refusals;
  - command validation, undo and redo;
  - the typed-number parser (accepts `O0012`);
  - per-op numbering;
  - a live post writes `O0077 (Lid)`, and undo restores O0001;
  - round-trip: a v58 file loads with nothing set, and a corrupt value is refused.
- **Also new:** `mcp_setup::set_program_states_undoes_and_refuses_by_name`, and ui `program_info_tests` (typing into the fields, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y, a refusal).
- **Gate:** 35 app test binaries (338 tests) pass, including conformance, golden_cl, posting, every post suite, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, mcp and mcp_setup. All camcraft-post tests pass. ui lib passes 378; the one failure is the headless-GPU test, which also fails on this machine without the change. Clippy (post/app/ui, `-D warnings`) is clean. **No golden changed.**

## Not exercised
A GUI hands-on check, and a run of a numbered program on a control or in the Hub. G-code changes only when a number or comment is set.

Changelog: The document states its program number and comment (Post page, MCP set_program); each post writes it in its own dialect - O-word (Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak, Haas), Heidenhain program name, SINUMERIK %_N_..._MPF, PathPilot header comment; project v59 (#258)

title: feat(motion,app): Trochoidal slot - engagement-controlled trochoid operation (#220 slice 1)
body:
Slice 1 of #220: an engagement-controlled trochoid generator and a standalone **Trochoidal slot** operation. Branched from upstream/main; the fork is synced at v0.15.0.

## What changed
**The generator** (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/trochoid_slot.rs`, `trochoid_loops.rs`, `trochoid_air.rs`), specced from Otkur & Lazoglu 2007 and Rauch, Duc & Hascoet 2009.
- **Loop shape:** each loop is the front arc of a circle of radius ρ = B / cos 10°, with B = (W − D)/2 by default. The arc runs wall to wall and meets each wall at 10°.
  - On a straight chain the loops are shifted copies, so they never cross. Classic full-circle trochoids always cross the previous loop, and the verifier holds the post on a same-depth crossing.
  - A wall move between arcs cleans the cusp, and a fillet (the smoothing radius) blends it into each arc.
- **Start and end:** a helical bore of radius B at the start. A stepped fan of arcs closes the far end.
- **Returns:** microlift (default 0.3 mm, retracing the arc just cut at the return feed) or retract.
- **Engagement:** measured with the Adaptive pins' dexel yardstick (`quality::measure`) on each candidate level. The planner tries steps from 100% of the user's step down to 7%, and a note says when the step was cut. Adaptive's planner raster was not reused because it counts finished walls as contact (see the decision file).
- **Lifted returns over air:** a new `machining2d::lifted_cut` checks each lifted return against the in-process stock.
- **Refused by name:**
  - a channel narrower than the tool (it suggests a plain Slot);
  - a loop wider than the room;
  - a limit no step can hold (the message gives the lowest reading, where it was, and at which step);
  - a loop leaving the channel;
  - a crossing (the verifier's own `crossed_pairs`);
  - a lifted return over stock.

**The operation:** `OpType::TrochoidalSlot` (kind 39) in the ribbon's 2D mill family.
- **Authoring:** two endpoints and a width, like Slot, verified against the slot's stadium.
- **Parameters:** loop width (auto), forward step, max engagement, return, microlift height, smoothing radius, stock to leave, heights, stepdown, cutting/return/plunge feeds, climb.
- **Undo and editing:** create and edit are undoable (`CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams`). It has a small Geometry/Heights/Passes/Feeds page.
- **Project file:** a `trochoidal_slot` params entry. There is no `PROJECT_VERSION` bump, following the probe op's precedent (#108/#344) for an appended kind. Older builds won't read a document that uses the new kind.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/220-trochoidal-slot.md`.

## How tested
- **motion `trochoid_slot`** (7 tests, plus 2 unit tests):
  - A full-width slot (D10 in W16, 1 mm step) measures θmax **66.5°**; a straight Slot in the same channel measures **180°**.
  - A 60° limit forces the step down, and the note says so.
  - The verifier is clean (no crossing, gouge or rapid-in-stock) for climb and conventional, microlift and retract.
  - Microlift returns land on air, and the check catches one placed over stock.
  - Named refusals; the loops post as arcs.
- **app `trochoid_op`:** create and edit undo/redo; generate verifies clean and posts G03; a too-narrow channel is refused by name; project round trip.
- **New goldens:** `golden/trochoid_slot_small.cl` and `golden/nc/trochoid_slot_small.nc` (Fanuc, G02/G03).
- **Edited tests:** `ribbon` and `probe_op` pinned the probe as the last kind; they now pin index 38, and kind 39 is pinned.
- **Passing:**
  - motion `adaptive_band`;
  - app mill2d_b/c, ribbon, tool_law, probe_op, golden_cl, fanuc_post, project_roundtrip, operations, commands_undo, conformance, heidenhain_block_form, slot_caps, drill_prior_kinds, pick_doors, setup_align, wall_column_gouge, drilling_axial;
  - ui kind/ribbon/tab tests (including `every_registry_kind_gets_its_tab_bar`) and ui `operations`;
  - clippy on motion, app and ui (`-D warnings`).
- **Runtime:** the `trochoid_slot` binary takes about 80 s in debug when run in parallel. Each test is under 25 s alone.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **No run yet:** a GUI hands-on check, and a Hub or machine run of the posted arcs. This adds new posted G-code.
- **Deferred to later slices:** Adaptive's trochoidal mode (Done means 2), the corner-overload pin, centre-line picking from a model chain (typed endpoints today), the in-plane cutting return, feed reduction where engagement rises, and wall finishing when the loop band is narrower than the room.

title: feat(post): EDM condition table as user data in the .mch edm section
body:
**Stacked on #551** (EDM machine kinds). Its commits show here until #551 merges; this PR adds one commit on top.

## What changed

`edm.conditions[]` in the `.mch` `edm` section (#531, part of #290, design D4):
- Each condition is `{ id, name, gap, wire_diameter | undersize, role: rough|skim|finish, notes }`. It holds only the geometry a toolpath needs. Power and flushing stay the control's, selected by `id`.
- `id` is the control's own selector, required and unique; a numeric id reads as its word. Lengths scale with the file's unit. Gap and undersize may be 0; a wire diameter must be positive.
- A garbled entry refuses the file, naming its id, and `is_sane` restates the law for project files.
- `Edm::condition(machine, id, need)` is the door the first EDM op (#532) calls at command creation. A missing condition, or an unstated field the op needs (gap, wire diameter, undersize), is refused by name before any generator runs.
- No conditions ship. Tests use an explicitly synthetic table.

## How tested

- New `edm_conditions`, 6/6:
  - a stated table reads, and the template states none;
  - an inch file's gap reads in mm;
  - the lookup refuses a missing condition or field by name;
  - eight garbled tables each refuse the file;
  - a hand-edited project machine with duplicate ids or a NaN gap is not sane;
  - the table rides the project file.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick`, escalated to batch: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app are green, and clippy `-D warnings` is clean on all 8 crates. ui: only the five known reds that are also red on main.
- Named: `edm_machine` 7, `machine` 32, `machine_library` 11, and `camcraft-post` all pass.

## Not exercised

- An EDM op using the door; that is #532.
- A real control's condition numbers; the data is the user's.

title: feat(post): wire_edm and sinker_edm machine kinds and the .mch edm section
body:
## What changed

The first EDM sub-issue of #290 (design D1):
- **Machine kinds.** `Kind::WireEdm` / `Kind::SinkerEdm`, declared only (`wire_edm`, `sinker_edm`, plus synonyms such as `wedm` and `die-sinker`). No axis inventory infers an EDM. The required axes are X+Y for wire and Z for sinker. A blank EDM machine has no spindle or coolant.
- **`.mch` `edm` section** (`crates/post/src/machine/edm.rs`). Wire: lower and upper guide planes, max taper, wire diameters, AWT. Sinker: orbit patterns (CamCraft's geometry name plus the control's word), max orbit radius, pickup. Every key is optional and absent means not stated. Lengths scale with the file's unit. A garbled value refuses the file by name, and the same law is restated in `is_sane` for project files.
- **No current op family admits an EDM**, so every op is refused at the door on an EDM setup.
- **Post-time family gate (safety).** `op_streams` now re-checks every op's family against its own setup's machine and refuses by name. Before this, an op made on a mill still posted in a milling dialect after its setup was remounted onto a lathe or an EDM; the door only guarded creation.
- **No EDM post serves yet** (`post_serves` is false for both kinds).
- **Templates are test fixtures for now.** The empty wire/sinker templates live in `crates/app/tests/edm/` because every library machine must have a post. They join the library with #533 / #542.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the kinds and the section.

## How tested

- New `edm_machine`, 7/7: templates parse and declare their kinds; a filled section reads and inch-scales; nine garbled values each refuse by name; the kind words round-trip and unknown kinds still refuse; no milling op enters an EDM setup; **a milling op remounted onto an EDM is refused at post, and undo restores the post**; a project round-trips the section.

title: feat(ui): detect pockets and slots on the Model page and create their operations
body:
Was stacked on #512 (pocket and slot recognition), which merged on 2026-11-10; this PR now holds only its own two commits against main.

## What changed

The Model page gains a **Pockets and slots** section (#511):
- **Detect pockets / slots** runs `app::recognize::pockets_of` once per click.
- Each recognised feature is a row: kind, slot width/length/ends, floor Z, depth, tightest corner, islands.
- Each row has a **Create Pocket / Create Slot** button. It queues one `CreateOperation`, selects the new op and opens its page, as one undo step. The button's tooltip names the tool it will use (the last document tool that fits the kind, the ribbon's quick-add rule). With no tool it is disabled.
- The scan is view state keyed by model and document version. Any document change hides the list, and Create refuses ("detect pockets again"), so no row offers coordinates the part no longer has.

The planning (name, seed, tool-sized helix, feature mapping) moved into `app::recognize::plan_operation`, with the shared seed in `operation::seed_params`. The MCP `detect_pockets {create}` tool calls the same code, so a click and an agent create the same operation. `ui` holds no recognition logic (layering ui → app).

## How tested

- New `pockets_tests` (ui lib), 4/4:
  - `detect_lists_the_slot_and_the_pocket`: a part with a through slot and a closed pocket lists both, with the right row text.
  - `create_adds_each_operation_as_one_undo_step`: the slot becomes a Slot cutting into the stock and the pocket a Pocket on the part's floor face, each opens its page, and one Undo removes each.
  - `a_changed_document_makes_the_list_stale`
  - `a_model_without_geometry_is_refused_by_name`
- `scripts/gate.sh quick`, escalated to batch, 812 s: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app all green. This includes `mcp`, `mcp_pockets`, `pocket_recognition`, `operations` and `project_roundtrip`, so the moved seed is behaviour-identical.

- clippy `-D warnings` on app and ui is clean after the follow-up commit.

- Clicking the section in a running GUI. The ui state tests drive the same methods the page calls.
- Hover-highlighting each floor in the viewport. It is left out (see the decision record) and can be a follow-up if wanted.

title: feat(app): raise fixture-striking links and retracts over the steel
body:
Was stacked on #476 (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh), which merged on 2026-11-09; this PR now targets main alone. Slice 5 of #339 per the triage on the issue: link and retract routing around fixtures.

## What changed
New `crates/app/src/operation/fixture_route.rs`, with one hook in `generate.rs` before the verify pass. It runs for upright mill paths only.

**The rule:**
- **What a link is:** the longest run of straight rapids between two non-rapid moves, or a path end.
- **When it counts as struck:** the gate's own fixture laws flag it. That's #464's whole-stack law (d2) plus #476's mesh acquittal, so a routed link is judged exactly as the post gate will judge it.
- **The fix:** a struck link becomes three G0 moves: up at its start XY, across, down to its end. The height is the higher of the link's own top and the highest box top under the traverse plus 5 mm (`ROUTE_GAP`). "Under the traverse" means every box the widest band reaches along the XY segment.
- **The cap:** the machine's stated Z stroke (WCS origin Z plus the top of the stroke), keeping at least 0.5 mm over the steel. Steel taller than that **refuses generation by name**: "the link at moves i..j … cannot clear fixture 'Clamp1': its steel stands to Z …, and the machine's Z stroke tops out at Z …". With no stroke stated there is no cap, as everywhere else.
- **Re-judging:** the re-laid link is judged again. If it's still struck, the steel stands over the link's own end column and no height helps. The link is then left as laid, its `FixtureHit` still blocks the post by name, and a path note says why.
- **Notes:** every raised link gets a path note: how many rose, from where, over which fixture, to what Z.

**Left as today (report-only):**
- **Keep-down feed links.** In the CL stream they look exactly like cuts, so lifting one could silently skip a cut. They're only taken inside the cut area, so if one hits steel the cuts beside it hit too, and the post is refused anyway. A keep-down **rapid** run at depth does become retract, traverse and plunge.
- **Other paths:** posed and rotary paths, lathe tools, paths with canned cycles (a traverse inserted between holes could post as a drill), thread or probe records, and runs inside a compensated span.

**Posted G-code changes only** for documents with a link the fixture laws strike, and only those links' G0 moves. Documents without fixtures return early untouched, and links that already clear are never rewritten, so all goldens are unchanged.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-routing.md`

## How tested
- **New app `fixture_route`** (6 tests):
  - A Contour around two blocks with a strap clamp to Z 40 between them, at clearance 25. As generated, the gate refuses ("strikes a fixture"). After the fix, the links rise to Z 45, the post is clean, the cuts are identical, and the note names Clamp1.
  - A clamp the links already clear leaves the path byte for byte.
  - A 100 mm Z stroke still routes over the 40 mm clamp, while a 400 mm clamp refuses generation naming 'Clamp1' and "Z 400.000".
  - A stay-down rapid link becomes retract, traverse and plunge. Clear steel and no steel are untouched.
  - Steel over a link's own end is left as laid and said.
  - A ceiling under the steel refuses, and a ceiling over it caps the rise.
- **Existing suites keep their verdicts:** fixtures (14), fixture_mesh (3), fixture_law_gaps (3), posting (17), tool_body (8). All app test binaries passed in the quick gate.
- `clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
This changes posted G-code (raised G0 links) for documents with struck fixtures, so it's a draft until a Hub or machine run. It needs a project with a clamp between features.

Changelog: Links and retracts that would strike a fixture are raised over the steel (a clamp taller than the machine's Z stroke refuses generation by name) instead of only being reported (#339)
